I hope I'm not breaking any news, but the school board did adopt a 2028/29 calendar at last night's meeting. You may have seen. I wanted to tick through some of the highlights of the calendar that were based on

community feedback that was received. So we heard loud and clear from teachers and parents as well that people really prefer that Thursday/Friday start to the school year to ease in. There are always contrary opinions on the calendar, so I also heard from people who would prefer Monday through Friday. But, I think the majority felt, especially our teachers, that was helpful for the students to ease into the year. So the school year's starting August 17th on Thursday. Thursday/Friday.

And one of the things I like most about the calendar that we ultimately adopted is that the second quarter ends before winter break. This means that the break's actually going to feel like a break for all of our students. There's not going to be projects hanging over people's heads. And the winter break, following some amendments at last night's meeting, is going to be a full two weeks. That was also feedback that we received. Again, there are some folks who would prefer a shorter winter break.

But I think the majority, at this time at least, wanted the full two weeks. Another element that I think probably the biggest piece of feedback we heard from educators and from families was that they were feeling squeezed on both sides of the calendar, that the summer was shrinking, and particularly going well into June was not the most productive instructionally. So, we are ending the school year Friday, June 1st.

And to the extent that there are days on either side of that summer, we felt it was more helpful to have that at the beginning of the year because our AP teachers and really any classroom that's teaching to a test at the end of the year, whether it's SOL or AP, finds that having that additional instructional time is really useful. And then finally, we balanced eliminating floating days or additional days that

happened during the course of the year to maximize the amount of five-day full instructional weeks that we have, while also recognizing the four cultural and religious holidays that we've observed the last few years. So you'll see that those are still included in the calendar, and for me, that was really important. My zip code where I live, we have one of the highest concentrations of Indian Americans in the United States, and if all students who are entitled to take an excused absence

were to take one on Diwali, for instance, you could have well over a quarter of the class missing, and for me, there's a lot of operational concerns there about learning loss and lesson planning. I know different communities across the county are different. But I think the majority of the board felt that it was helpful to keep these holidays, not only from a neighborliness respect for each of the different communities that live here in Loudoun, but also just that it made the most sense
